hook: Christopher Ré runs Stanford's Hazy Research lab, which has spent more than a decade turning ideas about data quality and hardware efficiency into companies. His early work on DeepDive, a system for pulling structured facts out of unstructured dark data, won him a MacArthur Fellowship in 2015. He later co-founded Snorkel AI to make labeling training data programmatic instead of manual, and Together AI, alongside collaborators including Tri Dao, Ce Zhang and Percy Liang, to build infrastructure for training and running open foundation models. Along the way his lab's systems work on hardware-aware training has fed directly into how modern language models are trained and served at scale.
